tagline: Through the Joshua trees, past Nothing, over Burro Creek.
intro: About 20 miles north of Wickenburg, US 93 enters a dense forest of Joshua trees, the largest of the yuccas, which the Mormon pioneers are said to have named for a prophet waving them on with upraised arms. Driving north, the Joshuas thin out among stacked boulders and the desert turns from Mojave to Sonoran.

Then the country gets mountainous, with Burro Creek, the Big Sandy River and Kaiser Springs in view, and so it stays all the way to Wikieup, a small community in the Big Sandy valley between the Hualapai and Aquarius mountains.

moments.title: Joshua forest
moments.text: Each tree depends on a single kind of moth to carry its pollen, and the moth's larvae depend on the tree's seeds. Neither gets on without the other.

moments.title: Nothing
moments.text: A gas station settlement founded in 1977 that reached a population of four at its height. Locals told travelers it got named by a bunch of drunks. It has been abandoned twice.

moments.title: Burro Creek
moments.text: The highway crosses on twin steel arches about 400 feet above an intermittent stream, and there is a campground of the same name.
